name: Nan Madol: Ceremonial Centre of Eastern Micronesia
description: Nan Madol is a ruined city built on more than 100 artificial islets in a lagoon off Pohnpei's southeast coast, linked by tidal canals that earn it the nickname "Venice of the Pacific." Between 1200 and 1500 CE, builders stacked huge basalt and coral boulders into walls around palaces, temples and tombs. Silt and spreading mangroves now threaten the ruins.
